label: Game Asset Formats
description: What a game actually needs delivered — a sprite sheet, a tileset, an icon grid, a turnaround. Each states the technical shape (grid, alignment, background) that makes the art usable rather than merely pretty.

items.name: pixel-sprite-sheet
items.text: a pixel-art sprite sheet: one character in a row of animation frames on a transparent grid, strict limited palette, crisp unfiltered pixels and no anti-aliasing
items.text_short: pixel sprite sheet, animation row, no AA

items.name: isometric-tile
items.text: an isometric tile: 2:1 diamond footprint aligned to the grid, art contained inside the tile with nothing overhanging, matte shading with a single light direction

items.name: ui-icon-set
items.text: a UI icon set: a grid of matching icons at one weight and one corner radius, each centred in its own square with equal optical padding, flat single-colour
items.text_short: UI icon grid, one weight, flat

items.name: item-icon-grid
items.text: an inventory item icon grid: each object rendered three-quarter on a plain dark cell with a soft contact shadow, consistent scale and light across the sheet
items.text_short: inventory icon grid, three-quarter, dark cells

items.name: character-turnaround
items.text: a character turnaround sheet: the same figure front, three-quarter, side and back in one row, feet on a shared baseline, neutral pose and even flat lighting

items.name: tileset-terrain
items.text: a terrain tileset: a seamless set of edge and corner pieces that mate on every side, consistent material and light, laid out as a labelled grid
items.text_short: seamless terrain tileset, edge and corner

items.name: parallax-layer
items.text: a parallax background layer: one horizontal band of scenery that repeats left to right without a visible seam, depth carried by value not detail

items.name: portrait-bust-ui
items.text: a dialogue portrait bust: head and shoulders framed for a small UI window, strong silhouette, expression readable at thumbnail size
